description.comment: The Spiroplasma endosymbiont of Glossina fuscipes fuscipes; sGff, naturally present in some wild Glossina fuscipes fuscipes populations and 50% of the Glossina fuscipes fuscipes colony flies at the FAO/IAEA IPCL, is of biological interest due to its ability to manipulate tsetse physiology. Flies used for the initiation of the preculture were derived from a high Spiroplasma prevalence Glossina fuscipes fuscipes (Gff) laboratory line, maintained at the insectary at FAO/IAEA Insect Pest Control Laboratory (IPCL) in Seibersdorf, Austria. Fly hemolymph was extracted from 10 surface-sterilized females and 10 males aged seven to 21 days by removing one front leg and aspirating the exposed hemolymph droplet with a 10 ul pipette tip. Precultures were initiated in three biological replicates by inoculating 3.2 ml preculture media (BSK-H + 5% filtered fly extract) with 10 ul of harvested hemolymph and incubated at 25 C for 14 days without agitation under microaerobic atmospheric conditions (8-9% O2, 7-8% CO2). Precultures were pelleted by centrifugation for 40 min at 2000g, resuspended in 3.2 ml of BSK-H-spiro media (BSK-H + 7.5% fly extract, 6% rabbit serum, 0.5% Penicillin, 2.5% arginine, 5% lipid mix) and aliquots of 100 ul stored at -80 C. Cultures were prepared using 100 ul frozen preculture aliquots in 3.2 ml of BSK-H-spiro media at 25 C in microaerobic conditions without agitation for the establishment of active long-term cultures.
